learn.title: Green Bonds: Funding Climate Projects
learn.intro: Green bonds are specialized financial instruments channeling investor capital into climate-positive projects like solar farms and wind parks. As governments and corporations commit to net-zero goals, these bonds have become critical for scaling renewable energy investments globally. Understanding how they work reveals the financial engine driving the clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: India issued its inaugural sovereign green bond in 2023, raising $1 billion for renewable energy projects. The initiative supports the country’s target of 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030. State-owned NTPC and REC Limited have also launched green bonds totaling over $4 billion for solar parks and wind farms.
learn.c2_text: Renewable developers issue green bonds to raise long-term capital for solar and wind projects. Investors receive regular interest payments, similar to corporate bonds, but with environmental impact. These bonds often carry lower interest rates due to government backing or multilateral guarantees, reducing project financing costs significantly.
learn.stat1: Global green bond issuance reached $532 billion in 2023
learn.stat2: India aims to raise $10 billion through green bonds by 2025
learn.stat3: Renewable projects using green bonds see 15% lower financing costs
learn.stat4: Over 30 countries have issued sovereign green bonds since 2019

learn.title: HVDC: Long-Distance Power Transmission
learn.intro: High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission lines enable efficient electricity transfer across vast distances—connecting remote renewable resources to urban demand centers. Unlike traditional AC systems, HVDC minimizes energy loss over thousands of kilometers. Mastering HVDC technology is key to unlocking continent-scale renewable integration.
learn.c1_text: India is building 33 GW of HVDC transmission capacity under its Green Energy Corridor program. The ±800 kV Raigarh-Pugalur line transmits 6,000 MW from Chhattisgarh's solar parks to Tamil Nadu. This infrastructure will evacuate renewable energy from resource-rich states to high-demand regions efficiently.
learn.c2_text: HVDC systems use voltage converters to transform AC to DC for transmission, then back to AC at destination. This process allows precise grid control, prevents cascading failures, and enables asynchronous connections between different grids. Modern VSC (Voltage Source Converter) technology further enhances flexibility for weak grids.

learn.stat2: India plans 15 GW HVDC capacity by 2030
learn.stat3: HVDC reduces transmission losses by up to 50% over 1,000 km
learn.stat4: The world's longest HVDC line spans 3,324 km in China

learn.title: Renewable Purchase Obligation Explained
learn.intro: India's Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) mandates that utilities source a minimum percentage of power from renewable sources. This policy mechanism drives demand for clean energy projects while ensuring grid integration. Understanding RPO dynamics reveals how regulatory frameworks accelerate India's renewable energy transition and protect investor interests.
learn.c1_text: Despite ambitious targets, many DISCOMs struggle with RPO compliance due to financial constraints. In 2023, utilities across 15 states defaulted on renewable energy purchases worth $2.8 billion. The government introduced relaxations and extended timelines to ensure continued renewable energy growth while supporting utility viability.
learn.stat1: India's total RPO target: 175 billion units by 2022

learn.stat3: Current renewable energy RPO compliance rate: 87%
learn.stat4: Rooftop solar RPO target: 40,000 MW by 2022

learn.title: ISTS Waiver: Boosting Renewable Economics
learn.intro: India's Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) waiver policy eliminates transmission charges for renewable energy projects, dramatically reducing their cost of electricity. This strategic intervention has made renewable power more competitive and accelerated grid connectivity for large-scale solar and wind farms across states.
learn.c1_text: Launched in 2017, the ISTS waiver was initially for solar projects commissioned by June 2020. Due to pandemic delays, it was extended multiple times—now covering projects commissioned by June 2025. Over 45 GW of renewable capacity has benefited, with developers saving approximately $1.2 billion in transmission charges.

learn.stat2: Tariff reduction: up to 25 paise/kWh for developers
learn.stat4: Waiver extended to June 2025 for solar and wind projects

learn.title: Wind Turbine Lifecycle and Recycling
learn.intro: Modern wind turbines operate for 25-30 years, but their composite blades pose unique recycling challenges at end-of-life. As global wind capacity expands, managing blade disposal becomes critical for sustainable energy transition. Understanding turbine longevity and blade recycling innovations ensures wind power remains truly green throughout its entire lifecycle.
learn.c1_text: India's first wind turbine blade recycling plant opened in Gujarat in 2023, processing 50,000 tons annually. Companies like Suzlon are developing blade-to-blade recycling methods. The government offers 30% capital subsidies for recycling facilities under its circular economy mission, supporting domestic waste management infrastructure.

learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Tapping Earth's Heat
learn.intro: Geothermal energy harnesses Earth's internal heat for electricity generation and direct heating applications. Unlike intermittent solar and wind, geothermal provides consistent baseload power 24/7. This reliable renewable source offers unique advantages for sustainable heating and cooling, making it essential for deep decarbonization strategies worldwide.
learn.c1_text: India has 338 hot springs across 12 states, with estimated geothermal potential of 10 GW. The government launched its National Geothermal Program in 2023, identifying 10 priority locations. Pilot projects in Himachal Pradesh and Gujarat aim to demonstrate 50 MW capacity by 2027, supporting clean heating in mountainous regions.
